meta.summary: Each of the 5 session stages pairs what you SEE with what happens INSIDE (the code path that produces it). Click a stage's two rows to compare altitudes; the bottom groups are always-on behaviors and engine internals that span every stage. Lanes are the agents + the shared machinery they coordinate through; edge labels cite the real mechanism at file:line.

findings.title: Deferred tool discovery is documented, not built
findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE_PATTERNS.md section 2 specs a Claude-Code-style ToolSearch meta-tool + deferred tool names. Zero implementing code. ACT uses static per-role tool subsets + the act CLI instead.
findings.evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE_PATTERNS.md:26-41; grep ToolSearch over act-agent = 0 hits

findings.title: 9 of 25 native Go client methods are unwired
findings.summary: internal/act/client.go mirrors the full server API but task-exec/file-lock/retry/abandon/pvm-search/status methods have zero Go callers; those ops run in the JS runner and TS CLI. Dead code, not broken behavior.

findings.title: ChronLog SQLite mode silently no-ops
findings.summary: storageType 'sqlite' routes flush to an empty stub = data loss; dormant because default is jsonl.

findings.title: File locking is prompt-only
findings.summary: claim/release endpoints + Go client methods exist, but no agent calls claim before editing; enforcement is prompt-instructed only (the pre/post tool-hook enabler is unbuilt).

findings.title: QA synthesis persists a marker, not the deliverable
findings.summary: Synthesis stamps synthesizedAt + summary; the full assembled deliverable is never persisted.

findings.title: Socket.io dashboard handlers vestigial
findings.summary: Socket handlers exist with no client consumer; clients use REST /api/log.
findings.evidence: server/src/index.ts:1300+ socket handlers; clients poll GET /api/log

findings.title: No auth on the coordination server
findings.summary: Every REST/socket endpoint trusts the caller; no token/identity check. Localhost-only trust boundary.

findings.title: Persistent vector store build-excluded (intentional)
findings.summary: Qdrant adapter exists but is excluded from the build; runtime uses in-memory local embeddings rebuilt from JSONL each boot. Deliberate (ops burden).

components.label: Human
components.detail: The only human entry; converses with the Planner in the TUI.
components.hover: You — the person typing in the terminal. The only human entry point; you talk to the Planner. From a user perspective, this is you giving instructions and reading answers.

components.label: Planner
components.detail: The ONLY agent that talks to the human. Runs INTAKE, decomposes the project into CREATE_TASK specs and routes them; evidence-based routing via PVM. planner.go.
components.hover: The Planner — your conversational partner and the only decision-maker. It interviews you, then breaks the project into tasks and assigns them. From a user perspective, this is the agent you talk to.

components.label: Intake / brownfield
components.detail: detectProjectState (404 vs 200 vs brownfield), runBrownfieldOnboard, handleProjectBrief; greenfield 5-question vs brownfield 2-question, resume fold-in. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: At startup, works out whether this is a brand-new project, a resumed one, or existing code to analyze, and runs the right intro questions (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the 'getting to know your project' conversation when you begin.

components.label: Turn manager
components.detail: runAgentTurn drives every Tier-1 turn (5-min timeout); resolves the backend-agnostic agent.Service via getAgent(role) and calls .Run(). orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Runs a single agent's turn — hands it the prompt, waits for the reply, and cancels it if it runs past 5 minutes (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is what makes an agent actually take its turn and respond.

components.label: Task dispatch (2-pass)
components.detail: handlePlannerTaskDirectives: content-hash dedup, lazy swarm spawn, two-pass create (tasks first, then resolve title-deps to IDs). orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Takes the Planner's task list, drops duplicates, starts the worker agents, and creates the tasks in the right dependency order (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the moment your plan becomes assigned work.

components.label: Autoroute + window
components.detail: autoRoutePlannerV with a sliding window (5 per 10 min), fireWhenPlannerIdle; cleared on human input. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: When a background agent reports something, this nudges the Planner to respond — with a cap so it can't spiral into a loop (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is what lets the team react on its own without you prompting each step.

components.label: Message-ownership loop
components.detail: messageOwnershipLoop subscribes to message pub/sub, tags speaker, routes finished Planner msgs to brief/task handlers and Tier-1 reports to autoroute. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Watches every finished message, tags who said it, and routes it to the right next step (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the traffic controller keeping each agent's words attributed and acted on.

components.label: Coordination-event loop
components.detail: coordinationEventLoop (3s) -> GetLog(50) -> render events as chat system messages; task_failed escalates to Planner. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Every 3 seconds it pulls recent coordination events from the server and shows them in the chat as status updates (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the live activity feed of what the team is doing.

components.label: On-demand sections
components.detail: The Planner's lazy-loaded extra instructions: a registry (sections.go) maps 4 names -> provider fns (evidence_routing / success_criteria / validation / examples), expanded only when the Planner asks.
components.hover: Optional instruction blocks the Planner pulls in only when needed. From a user perspective, this keeps the Planner lean until it needs more detail.

components.label: Observer
components.detail: Silent background watchdog; only speaks on an anomaly (stuck tasks, stale locks, idle agents, bottlenecks). Makes no decisions. observer.go.
components.hover: The Observer — a silent watchdog that checks project health on a loop and only speaks when something looks wrong. From a user perspective, this is the team's early-warning system.

components.label: Observer loop
components.detail: observerLoop (120s): status snapshot, anomaly detection, Tier-1 watchdog; injects only on anomaly. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Every 2 minutes it quietly checks the project's health and only speaks up if something looks stuck or wrong (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the silent watchdog that flags problems.

components.label: Assurance
components.detail: Validates finished work against @success_criteria (95% gate); pass -> validated, fail -> back to the agent with gaps. Read-only tools. assurance.go.
components.hover: Assurance — the quality gate. It scores finished work against the success criteria and only passes it if it clears the bar. From a user perspective, this is the checker that keeps quality honest.

components.label: Validation router
components.detail: validationPollLoop (10s) -> checkPendingValidation -> routeToAssurance -> parseValidationVerdict (fail-closed) -> SubmitVerdict. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Every 10 seconds it picks up finished work and sends it to the Assurance agent to be checked against the success criteria (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the hand-off to quality control.

components.label: QA / Synthesizer
components.detail: Assembles Assurance-passed outputs into the final deliverable; emits SYNTHESIS_COMPLETE or NEED_CLARIFICATION. Read-only tools. qa_synthesizer.go.
components.hover: QA / Synthesizer — pulls the approved pieces into the final result. From a user perspective, this is the agent that produces what you receive.

components.label: QA router
components.detail: qaPollLoop (10s) -> checkValidatedTasks -> routeToQA -> parseSynthesisResponse -> SubmitSynthesis; NEED_CLARIFICATION forwarding. orchestrator.go.
components.hover: Every 10 seconds it takes work that passed checking and sends it to the QA agent to assemble the final result (orchestrator.go). From a user perspective, this is the step that pulls approved pieces into a deliverable.

components.label: Swarm roles (Tier 2)
components.detail: The five headless worker agents, each a role specialization with its own system prompt: developer (default), frontend_dev, backend_dev, qa_engineer, researcher.
components.hover: The swarm — the worker agents that build things, one per specialization. From a user perspective, this is your team of builders.

components.label: Spawner
components.detail: StartSwarm/startOneLocked: sweep orphans, find script + node, one process per role with its own group + log. spawner.go.
components.hover: Launches one worker process per role and supervises them (spawner.go). From a user perspective, this is what brings your team of worker agents online.

components.label: Register + self-heal
components.detail: POST /api/agents/register on startup; 409 -> delete + retry. act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: When a worker starts it signs in with the server, clearing any stale copy of itself first (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is a worker clocking in.

components.label: Runner poll loop
components.detail: main loop polls GET /api/tasks/assigned, executes, sleeps. act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: Each worker repeatedly asks the server 'any task for me?' and runs whatever it's given (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is a worker waiting for and picking up jobs.

components.label: Prompt build + brief
components.detail: buildTaskPrompt assembles brief + parallel + PVM + inbox + gap context; fetchAgentBrief diverges (claude-code on-disk short-circuit vs HTTP inject). act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: Builds the worker's full task prompt — the brief, related past work, teammates' context, its inbox — before it starts (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is what gives a worker everything it needs to begin.

components.label: runAgent switch
components.detail: runAgent() branches on BACKEND. [Fork B fan-out] act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: The worker's fork: run its task with the built-in binary or with Claude Code (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is the per-worker engine choice.

components.label: act-agent path
components.detail: runAgentActAgent: execFile the act-agent binary headless, parse {status,result}. [Fork B twin] act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: The default worker path — runs the task with the built-in ACT binary and reads back the result (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is a worker doing the job with the built-in engine.

components.label: claude-code path
components.detail: runAgentClaudeCode: claude --print --dangerously-skip-permissions. [Fork B twin] act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: The alternate worker path — runs the task with Claude Code (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is a worker doing the job with Claude Code.

components.label: Completion report
components.detail: reportComplete consumes the uniform {success,output,error,code} from either backend -> POST complete + submit-for-validation. [Fork B convergence] act-runner.mjs.
components.hover: Takes whatever either engine returned, reports the task complete, and submits it for checking (act-runner.mjs). From a user perspective, this is a worker turning in finished work.

components.label: REST front door
components.detail: Express routes for projects/tasks/agents/messages/files/pvm. server/src/index.ts.
components.hover: The front door of the coordination server — all the web endpoints the app and workers call (server/src/index.ts). From a user perspective, this is the switchboard everything talks through.

components.label: Task coordinator
components.detail: Task state machine, createTask, assignOptimalAgent, dependency/cycle handling. TaskCoordinator.ts.
components.hover: Tracks every task's state and assigns each one to the best-matching worker (TaskCoordinator.ts). From a user perspective, this is the project board that knows who's doing what.

components.label: Agent registry
components.detail: registerAgent, capability matching, health check. AgentRegistry.ts.
components.hover: Keeps the list of which agents are online and what each can do (AgentRegistry.ts). From a user perspective, this is the team roster.

components.label: Project + brief store
components.detail: In-memory projects + per-agent briefs; event-sourcing replay rebuilds on boot. index.ts.
components.hover: Holds the project details and each agent's brief in memory, rebuilt from the log on restart (index.ts). From a user perspective, this is where your project's setup lives.

components.label: File locks
components.detail: claim/release/locks; auto-release on completion or agent removal. index.ts.
components.hover: Lets a worker claim a file so two agents don't edit it at once (index.ts). From a user perspective, this is what stops agents stepping on each other's edits.

components.label: Event hub
components.detail: EventHub classifies messages, rate-limits, selects responder; Socket.io + A2A push. EventHub.ts / index.ts.
components.hover: Sorts and routes the messages agents send each other, with rate limits (EventHub.ts). From a user perspective, this is the team's messaging system.

components.label: Validation / synthesis routes
components.detail: submit-for-validation / pending-validation / validated / validation-verdict / synthesis. index.ts.
components.hover: The endpoints for submitting work, recording the pass/fail verdict, and the final assembly (index.ts). From a user perspective, this is the quality-control paper trail.

components.label: ChronLog
components.detail: Append-only event log; two append surfaces (REST handlers + EventHub); buffered flush to JSONL + per-project mirror. ChronologicalLog.ts.
components.hover: An append-only log of every coordination event, written to disk (ChronologicalLog.ts). From a user perspective, this is the project's permanent activity history.

components.label: PVM indexer
components.detail: indexNewEvents every 10s: dedup, buildEmbeddingText, embed, batchStore. PVMIndexer.ts.
components.hover: Every 10 seconds it turns new log events into searchable memory (PVMIndexer.ts). From a user perspective, this is what lets the team remember and reuse past work.

components.label: Vector store
components.detail: LocalEmbeddingVectorStore: MiniLM embeddings in an in-memory array; silent hash-embed fallback if the model fails to load. LocalEmbeddingVectorStore.ts.
components.hover: Holds those memories as searchable vectors, kept in memory (LocalEmbeddingVectorStore.ts). From a user perspective, this is the searchable memory bank.

components.label: PVM search
components.detail: GET /api/pvm/search; cross-project by default, opt-in project scope. index.ts.
components.hover: Lets an agent search past work for relevant context (index.ts /api/pvm/search). From a user perspective, this is an agent asking 'have we done something like this before?'

components.label: Analytics / self-improvement
components.detail: getAgentProfile / getAgentSynergy / compareAgents; SelfImprovementEngine reads real task-outcome events. index.ts / SelfImprovementEngine.ts.
components.hover: Works out each agent's skill profile and team-fit from real outcomes (SelfImprovementEngine.ts). From a user perspective, this is how the system learns which agents are good at what.

components.label: Priming / shim-note wrap
components.detail: makePrimingInjector/wrapPriming prepend the internal marker + do-not-respond header; renderShimNote injects the per-role allowed-subcommand list. app.go.
components.hover: For an agent running on an outside CLI, this packages its role instructions plus its allowed commands and sends them as the first message (app.go). From a user perspective, this is what briefs an external engine so it behaves like an ACT agent.

components.label: Backend switch
components.detail: App.New per-role switch on agents.<role>.backend: empty/act-agent -> in-process; external host -> ACP. app.go.
components.hover: The fork in the road: for each role it picks the built-in model or an outside CLI, based on your config (app.go). From a user perspective, this is the setting that decides what engine powers each agent.

components.label: In-process agent
components.detail: agent.NewAgent goroutine with scoped history (HistoryThread/None) + per-role tool subset. [Fork A twin] agent.go.
components.hover: The built-in path — runs an agent inside the app on the chosen model, with its own memory scope and tool set (agent.go). From a user perspective, this is the default, nothing-extra-to-install way an agent runs.

components.label: ACP agent
components.detail: acp.NewACPAgent drives an external CLI over ACP; lazy priming on first session. [Fork A twin] acp/agent.go.
components.hover: The outside-CLI path — drives an external assistant over a wire protocol as if it were a built-in agent (acp/agent.go). From a user perspective, this is how an agent runs on Claude Code or antigravity instead of the default.

components.label: ACP protocol layer
components.detail: client / transport / session: newline-framed JSON-RPC to the external CLI host. internal/acp/.
components.hover: The plumbing that talks to an outside CLI — opening a session, sending prompts, reading replies (internal/acp/). From a user perspective, this is the cable connecting ACT to an external assistant.

components.label: Tier-1 CLI shim
components.detail: act-tier1-<role> shim enforces the per-role CLI allowlist for ACP-backed Tier-1. cmd/act-tier1-shim/.
components.hover: A gatekeeper that limits which ACT commands an outside-CLI agent is allowed to run (act-tier1-shim). From a user perspective, this stops an external engine from doing more than its role should.

components.label: Per-role tool subsets
components.detail: Tier1ToolsForRole statically partitions tools per role (what ACT does instead of deferred discovery). agent/tools.go.
components.hover: Decides which tools each role may use, kept deliberately small to save tokens (tools.go). From a user perspective, this is why each agent only has the tools it needs.

components.label: External CLIs
components.detail: Outside agent CLIs driven over ACP as a Tier-1 or Tier-2 backend: Claude Code (claude --print) and antigravity/agy (in flight).
components.hover: Optional outside coding assistants that can power an agent instead of the built-in model. From a user perspective, swappable engines you can put behind an agent.
